# az-tf-mlz-dns-resolver

Azure DNS Private Resolver for Fortytwo's managed landing zone (MLZ): the resolver in a hub (or Virtual
WAN sidecar) virtual network, its inbound and outbound endpoints, and DNS forwarding rulesets with their
rules and virtual network links. AzAPI only, without telemetry.

- **Inbound endpoints** give on-premises DNS servers, a firewall's DNS proxy or a virtual network's DNS
  settings an address in the hub to send queries to; Azure DNS answers them, with the private DNS zones
  linked to the hub. Without `private_ip_address` Azure assigns the subnet's fifth address (`.4`); set
  it (for example `cidrhost(<subnet prefix>, 4)`) when the address must be known before apply.
- **Outbound endpoints** and **forwarding rulesets** send queries for chosen domains, from the virtual
  networks linked to a ruleset, to other DNS servers such as on-premises ones. The longest matching
  domain wins; other queries go to Azure DNS.

The module creates neither the virtual networks nor the endpoints' subnets: each endpoint needs a
subnet of its own in the resolver's virtual network, /28 to /24, delegated to
`Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers`.

## Layout

| Path | Resource type | Called |
|---|---|---|
| root | `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers` | |
| `modules/inbound_endpoint` | `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers/inboundEndpoints` | by the root, per `inbound_endpoints` entry |
| `modules/outbound_endpoint` | `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers/outboundEndpoints` | by the root, per `outbound_endpoints` entry |
| `modules/forwarding_ruleset` | `Microsoft.Network/dnsForwardingRulesets` | by the root, per `forwarding_rulesets` entry, or alone |
| `modules/forwarding_rule` | `Microsoft.Network/dnsForwardingRulesets/forwardingRules` | by the ruleset, or alone |
| `modules/virtual_network_link` | `Microsoft.Network/dnsForwardingRulesets/virtualNetworkLinks` | by the ruleset, or alone (a spoke linking itself) |

## Behaviour

- **Replacement:** Azure cannot change a resolver's virtual network, an endpoint's subnet or address, a
  rule's domain name or a link's virtual network; changing one replaces that resource. A ruleset's
  outbound endpoints, a rule's targets, state and metadata, a link's metadata and every tag are updated
  in place.
- **Locks:** the resolver's lock also covers its endpoints, and a ruleset's lock its rules and links; the
  module removes a lock around changes to what it covers. A `ReadOnly` lock still blocks updating the
  locked resource itself: remove it first.
- **Interfaces:** locks, role assignments and diagnostic settings on the resolver and on each ruleset,
  through [`az-tf-mlz-interfaces`](https://github.com/fortytwoservices/az-tf-mlz-interfaces). Neither
  type has log categories, so diagnostic settings take `metrics` (`AllMetrics`) only; Learn marks none of
  their metrics as exportable, so a setting may carry little. DNS query logs come from DNS security
  policies, which this module does not manage. Endpoints, rules and links take no interfaces.
- **Removing an outbound endpoint** takes two applies: first take it out of every ruleset's
  `outbound_endpoints`, then remove it. Azure deletes an outbound endpoint only once no ruleset uses it,
  and Terraform deletes a removed resource before it updates the resources that used it.
  `create_before_destroy` on the ruleset would reverse that order, but Terraform passes it on to the
  endpoints and the resolver: a locked resolver's endpoint would then be deleted after its lock is back
  (`ScopeLocked`), and replacing an endpoint or the resolver would need a new name.
- **Retries:** by default every write retries `AnotherOperationInProgress`, and `CannotDeleteResource`:
  Azure reports endpoints deleted while it still counts them as the resolver's nested resources for a
  short while.
- **Target ports:** Azure accepts only port 53 for a rule's target DNS servers.
- **Metadata on rules and links:** azapi compares only the keys in the body, so removing one entry
  would otherwise never reach Azure. The metadata is also sent through `sensitive_body`, versioned by a
  hash of the map, so any change is written. The cost: a plan that removes an entry shows only the
  version's hash changing, not which entry goes (added and changed entries still show in the body).
- **Loops:** do not link a ruleset to the virtual network of an inbound endpoint that one of its rules
  forwards to; the queries would loop.

### <a name="input_diagnostic_settings"></a> [diagnostic\_settings](#input\_diagnostic\_settings)

Description: A map of diagnostic settings to create on the resource. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the diagnostic setting. One will be generated if not set, however this will not be unique if you want to create multiple diagnostic setting resources.
- `logs` - (Optional) A set of log entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of a specific log category to enable. Mutually exclusive with `category_group`.
  - `category_group` - (Optional) The name of a log category group to enable (for example, `allLogs` or `audit`). Mutually exclusive with `category`.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the log entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the log entry.
    - `days` - (Optional) The retention period in days. Defaults to `0` (retain indefinitely).
    - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the retention policy is enabled. Defaults to `false`.
- `metrics` - (Optional) A set of metric entries to send to the destination. Each entry has the following attributes:
  - `category` - (Optional) The name of the metric category to enable.
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the metric entry is enabled. Defaults to `true`.
  - `retention_policy` - (Optional) The retention policy for the metric entry, with the same `days` and `enabled` attributes as `logs.retention_policy`.
- `log_analytics_destination_type` - (Optional) The destination type for the diagnostic setting. Possible values are `Dedicated` and `AzureDiagnostics`. Defaults to `Dedicated`.
- `workspace_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the log analytics workspace to send logs and metrics to.
- `storage_account_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the storage account to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_authorization_rule_resource_id` - (Optional) The resource ID of the event hub authorization rule to send logs and metrics to.
- `event_hub_name` - (Optional) The name of the event hub. If none is specified, the default event hub will be selected.
- `marketplace_partner_resource_id` - (Optional) The full ARM resource ID of the Marketplace resource to which you would like to send Diagnostic Logs.

### <a name="input_forwarding_rulesets"></a> [forwarding\_rulesets](#input\_forwarding\_rulesets)

Description: DNS forwarding rulesets the module creates in `parent_id`, by key, each through `modules/forwarding_ruleset` with its rules and virtual network links. A virtual network linked to a ruleset sends queries that match a rule to the rule's DNS servers, through the ruleset's outbound endpoints; other queries go to Azure DNS. The longest matching domain wins.

- `name` - Name of the ruleset. Changing it replaces the ruleset, its rules and its links.
- `outbound_endpoints` - One or two outbound endpoints of the resolver: keys of `outbound_endpoints`, or resource IDs.
- `rules` - (Optional) Forwarding rules, by rule name (letters, digits, underscores and hyphens, starting with a letter), at most 1,000:
  - `domain_name` - The DNS namespace forwarded, dot-terminated (`contoso.com.`), or `.` for every name. Changing it replaces the rule.
  - `target_dns_servers` - 1 to 6 DNS servers, `ip_address` and `port` (defaults to `53`), tried in order. Not Azure DNS (`168.63.129.16`).
  - `enabled` - (Optional) Whether the rule applies. Defaults to `true`.
  - `metadata` - (Optional) Metadata on the rule.
- `virtual_network_links` - (Optional) Virtual networks whose queries the rules apply to, by link name, at most 500: `virtual_network_id` (in this region, any subscription of the tenant; changing it replaces the link) and `metadata` (optional). Do not link the virtual network of an inbound endpoint that a rule forwards to: its queries would loop.
- `lock` - (Optional) A lock on the ruleset, as the module's `lock`. Azure applies it to the rules and links too, so the module removes it around their changes.
- `role_assignments` - (Optional) Role assignments on the ruleset, as the module's `role_assignments`.
- `diagnostic_settings` - (Optional) Diagnostic settings on the ruleset, as the module's `diagnostic_settings` (metrics only: a ruleset has no log categories).

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name               = string
    outbound_endpoints = list(string)
    rules = optional(map(object({
      domain_name = string
      target_dns_servers = list(object({
        ip_address = string
        port       = optional(number, 53)
      }))
      enabled  = optional(bool, true)
      metadata = optional(map(string), {})

    virtual_network_links = optional(map(object({

### <a name="input_inbound_endpoints"></a> [inbound\_endpoints](#input\_inbound\_endpoints)

Description: Inbound endpoints, by key: the IP addresses that on-premises DNS servers, a firewall's DNS proxy or a virtual network's DNS settings send queries to, answered by Azure DNS with the private DNS zones linked to the resolver's virtual network. At most 5.

- `name` - Name of the endpoint.
- `subnet_id` - Resource ID of its subnet in `virtual_network_id`: /28 to /24, delegated to `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers`, used by no other endpoint or service.
- `private_ip_address` - (Optional) A static IPv4 address in the subnet. When null Azure assigns the subnet's fifth address (`.4` in `10.0.0.0/28`). Set it when the address must be known before apply, for example `cidrhost(<subnet prefix>, 4)`.

Changing an endpoint's subnet or address replaces it.

Type:

    name               = string
    subnet_id          = string
    private_ip_address = optional(string)
  }))
```

### <a name="input_outbound_endpoints"></a> [outbound\_endpoints](#input\_outbound\_endpoints)

Description: Outbound endpoints, by key: where queries matching a forwarding ruleset's rules leave the virtual network for their target DNS servers. At most 5.

- `name` - Name of the endpoint.
- `subnet_id` - Resource ID of its subnet in `virtual_network_id`: /28 to /24, delegated to `Microsoft.Network/dnsResolvers`, used by no other endpoint or service. Changing it replaces the endpoint.

Azure deletes an outbound endpoint only once no ruleset uses it, and Terraform deletes a removed endpoint before it updates the rulesets that used it. So remove an endpoint from every ruleset's `outbound_endpoints` in one apply, and from this map in the next; removing a ruleset together with its endpoints works in one apply.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name      = string
    subnet_id = string
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_retry"></a> [retry](#input\_retry)

Description: Retry configuration applied to every `azapi` resource managed by the module and its submodules. Defaults retry `AnotherOperationInProgress`, which Azure returns while another write to the resolver or its virtual network runs, and `CannotDeleteResource`, which Azure returns for a resolver whose endpoints it has just reported deleted but still counts as nested resources; any field can be overridden.

- `error_message_regex`  - (Optional) A list of regex patterns matching error messages that trigger a retry. Defaults to `["AnotherOperationInProgress", "CannotDeleteResource"]`.
- `interval_seconds`     - (Optional) Initial interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `30`.
- `max_interval_seconds` - (Optional) Maximum interval between retries in seconds. Defaults to `300`.

See <https://registry.terraform.io/providers/Azure/azapi/latest/docs/resources/resource#retry> for full semantics.

Type:

```hcl
object({
    error_message_regex  = optional(list(string), ["AnotherOperationInProgress", "CannotDeleteResource"])
    interval_seconds     = optional(number, 30)
    max_interval_seconds = optional(number, 300)
  })
```

Default: `{}`

### <a name="input_role_assignments"></a> [role\_assignments](#input\_role\_assignments)

Description: A map of role assignments to create on the DNS private resolver. The map key is deliberately arbitrary to avoid issues where map keys maybe unknown at plan time.

- `name` - (Optional) The name of the role assignment. If not set, a random UUID will be generated. Changing this forces the creation of a new resource.
- `role_definition_id_or_name` - The ID or name of the role definition to assign to the principal.
- `principal_id` - The ID of the principal to assign the role to.
- `description` - (Optional) The description of the role assignment.
- `skip_service_principal_aad_check` - (Optional) If set to true, skips the Azure Active Directory check for the service principal in the tenant. Defaults to false.
- `condition` - (Optional) The condition which will be used to scope the role assignment.
- `condition_version` - (Optional) The version of the condition syntax. Leave as `null` if you are not using a condition, if you are then valid values are '2.0'.
- `delegated_managed_identity_resource_id` - (Optional) The delegated Azure Resource Id which contains a Managed Identity. Changing this forces a new resource to be created. This field is only used in cross-tenant scenario.
- `principal_type` - (Optional) The type of the `principal_id`. Possible values are `User`, `Group` and `ServicePrincipal`. It is necessary to explicitly set this attribute when creating role assignments if the principal creating the assignment is constrained by ABAC rules that filters on the PrincipalType attribute.

> Note: only set `skip_service_principal_aad_check` to true if you are assigning a role to a service principal.

Type:

```hcl
map(object({
    name                                   = optional(string, null)
    role_definition_id_or_name             = string
    principal_id                           = string
    description                            = optional(string, null)
    skip_service_principal_aad_check       = optional(bool, false)
    condition                              = optional(string, null)
    condition_version                      = optional(string, null)
    delegated_managed_identity_resource_id = optional(string, null)
    principal_type                         = optional(string, null)
  }))
```

Default: `{}`

## Development

Tools: Terraform 1.17.0, TFLint 0.65.0, terraform-docs 0.24.0 (the versions CI uses).

| What | Command |
|---|---|
| Format, validate, lint, unit tests, README drift (what CI runs) | `scripts/check.sh` |
| Format the code and regenerate the READMEs first | `scripts/check.sh --fix` |
| Integration tests in Azure | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/integration.sh [dir ...]` |
| Examples: apply, plan again (must be empty), destroy | `ARM_SUBSCRIPTION_ID=<test subscription> scripts/e2e.sh [examples/<name> ...]` |

`README.md` files are generated from `_header.md`, the code and `_footer.md`; do not edit them by hand.

## Versions and releases

Every release is a SemVer tag `vX.Y.Z`; tags never move, and `main` is never consumed. Pin a release:

```hcl
source = "git::https://github.com/fortytwoservices/<repository>.git?ref=vX.Y.Z"
```

Pull requests are squash-merged, and their titles follow Conventional Commits, which set the next
version: `fix:` a patch, `feat:` a minor (a patch before 1.0.0), `feat!:` or `fix!:` a major (a minor
before 1.0.0). `docs:`, `test:`, `ci:`, `chore:` and `refactor:` release nothing. release-please keeps a
release pull request open; merging it writes `CHANGELOG.md`, the tag and the GitHub release.
